The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest in Chickmagalur Police Station, Crime No.15/2024, registered for the offences punishable under Sections, 406, 408, 418, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC which is pending on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Chikkamagaluru.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that the complainant is working as a senior manager at Louis Dreyfus Company India Private Limited, since last 10 years, and the said company is having its warehouse obtained on rent at the place belonging to C.N.Akmal at Mugulavalli Village,
Chikkamagaluru Taluk.

entities.text: Louis Dreyfus Company India Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is alleged that the company used to store coffee beans purchased from various sellers in and around Chikkamagaluru, and later on, he used to export the same.

According to the NC: 2024:KHC:10696 prosecution, the complainant is a Senior Manager with control over warehouses situated in Mugulavalli Village, Chikkamagaluru Taluk and one situated in Koppa Village, Piriyapattana Taluk.
The petitioner is a Supervisor of the warehouse situated in Magulavalli Village, since the year 2010, the other accused was assisting accused No.1/petitioner.

It is alleged that the other accused were required to give details of the coffee beans purchased and stocked in the said warehouse, and they have also executed a consent letter while joining the company.
According to the prosecution, on 19.11.2023 when the complainant along with the petitioner verified the stock stored in the warehouse, it was found to be accurate.
It is further alleged that, the same was entered in relevant records.

It is further alleged that the petitioner used to send the total weight of the coffee beans stored in the warehouse and on 04.12.2023 a statement showing that weight of the copy was forwarded by him through e-mail.
On perusing the same report, the complainant encountered doubt and then he reported the matter to his NC: 2024:KHC:10696 higher officers.
On 08.12.2023 at 10.30 a.m., he along with the petitioner, verified the stock which was actually stored and found that 46.803 of Metric tones of coffee beans were found missing.
On enquiry, the petitioner who is arraigned as an accused No.1 admitted that he had sold 23.216 of Metric tones of coffee beans illegally by giving a confessional letter.
The missing coffee beans were worth of Rs.1,24,96,447/- and in this regard a complaint was lodged.

3. On the basis of the complaint, FIR came to be registered and the petitioner apprehending his arrest has approached the learned Sessions Judge and the learned Sessions Judge has rejected his bail petition.
Hence, the petitioner is before this Court.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the records.
It is an undisputed fact that, the petitioner is a supervisor of the warehouse where the coffee beans were stored.

Since, the petitioner is a supervisor, it is his duty to give a proper account of the coffee beans, and now it is submitted that the duty of the petitioner is to overall manage the stock and weight and other things are concerned to the accounts department.

But the allegations disclose that 46.80 metric tones of coffee beans were found missing, and the allegations further discloses that the petitioner himself has given a confessional letter before the complainant wherein, he admitted that 23.216 metric tones of coffee beans are being sold by him illegally.

Since, the petitioner is the supervisor, and since he has admitted the entrustment, it is for him to explain how he disposed of these coffee beans and how such a huge difference in coffee beans was forthcoming.
Now it is simply asserted that, he has been made as a scape goat but he is prepared to explain what steps he has taken.
If he had found that there was any unlawful activities, he could have reported to the higher officer.

Apart from that NC: 2024:KHC:10696 he himself has given a confession statement wherein he admitted that, he has misappropriated 23.216 metric tones of coffee, and this statement is not denied specifically.

6. Considering these facts and circumstances, the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is essential to ascertain how this huge quantity of coffee beans was illegally transported and how they were disposed of, and who else were involved in this offence.
7. Considering these facts and circumstances question of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner does not arise at all.
Hence, the petition being devoid of any merits, does not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.
